content:
AIChatApp Authentication Reference

- Login is handled by POST /api/auth/login.
- Protected chat endpoints require Authorization: Bearer <token>.
- Gateway calls also require X-Api-Client and X-Api-Key.
- JWT generation and validation depend on JwtSettings:Issuer, JwtSettings:Audience, and JwtSettings:SecretKey.
- In local Web development, use the HTTPS Gateway URL https://localhost:7067/ for Frontend:GatewayBaseUrl to preserve Authorization headers on chat requests.

2FA flow:
- The user signs in, then calls POST /api/auth/2fa/setup to receive the authenticator setup data.
- The returned AuthenticatorUri or SharedKey is scanned or entered into Google Authenticator.
- POST /api/auth/2fa/verify confirms setup using a current 6-digit TOTP code.
- After 2FA is enabled, future login requests must include OtpCode.
- POST /api/auth/2fa/disable disables 2FA using a fresh authenticator code.
- POST /api/auth/2fa/status returns whether 2FA is enabled.
- TOTP codes are 6 digits and use a 30-second time window.

Common auth issue:
- 401 invalid_token usually means the JWT is stale, was issued by a different running stack, no longer matches the active JWT secret/config, or was dropped during HTTP-to-HTTPS Gateway redirection.
